content:
mira: Heads-up — seeing mTLS failures between us-east-1 txn-gateway and eu-west-1 model-router after cert rotation. Error in logs: "TLS handshake timeout" and "remote error: tls: bad certificate". No other infra changes.

kai: Can you paste the failing stack/openssl output? Is this inter-region peering or via public LB?

mira: It’s via our internal egress proxy (envoy) over peered VPCs. Quick openssl check shows cert chain mismatch: 
```
$ openssl s_client -connect model-router.eu-west-1.internal:443 -showcerts
CONNECTED(00000003)
depth=0 CN = model-router.eu-west-1.rw.internal
verify error:num=20:unable to get local issuer certificate
verify return:1
---
sslv3 alert handshake failure
140736820285136:error:14094410:SSL routines:ssl3_read_bytes:sslv3 alert handshake failure:ssl/record/rec_layer_s3.c:1543:SSL alert number 40
```

sanjay: Looks like the client is presenting a cert signed by the old CA or a rotated key. We rolled CA via certbot-bot yesterday for internal certs — @certbot-bot any events?

certbot-bot: automated: rotated CA root for internal certs at 2024-08-25T03:12:00Z, version bump v2 -> v3. Last pushed to secret-store: secret://kms/internal-ca/v3 (a/e role).

olivia: We pushed a config change to gateway to trust new CA bundle but looks like model-router still has v2 pinned in the sidecar cert list. Probably a rollout ordering issue.

julian: This is the classic CA-first vs clients-first rollout problem. If server is using certs signed by new CA but client trusts old only you get verify errors, or vice-versa. We should support cross-signed overlap for 48h during rotates.

mira: Agreed. For this incident, can we do a quick mitigation: 1) add v2 CA into gateway trust store, 2) re-deploy model-router sidecar with updated certs, 3) check KMS access logs for any failed decrypts?

kai: I can add v2 CA back to gateway trust within 5m. Suggest we also enable tls_debug logs on envoy to capture the exact presented certs: set TRACE on listener filter.

sanjay: KMS logs (from key-ring-us-east and eu-west KMS) show no decryption errors; secrets were readable. That implies cert material distributed but some nodes didn't pick up new secret version. Possibly stale secret-mount on host-level cache.

mira: Also seeing some TLS config hardening rules were recently applied (tls-min-version: TLS1.3, cipher preferences) in eu-west. Could be an incompatibility if an older sidecar hasn't been updated. Any config drift?

olivia: There was a canary where we enforced TLS1.3 on model-router in eu-west. Canary passed for 3 hosts but not rolled to all — so mixed cluster state. Combined with CA rotation, mismatch is likely.

julian: Action items:
- kai: re-add old CA to gateway trust (temporary).
- olivia: rollback TLS-min-version enforcement on model-router or patch sidecars to TLS1.3-compatible build.
- sanjay: confirm secret versions mounted on running pods and force a rolling restart if node cache stale.
- mira: run a cert fingerprint audit across regions and update runbook with cross-sign overlap requirement.

kai: Done — v2 CA re-added to gateway trust, rolled out via config version 2024-08-25T10:12Z. Monitoring TLS success rate. :white_check_mark:

mira: After kai change, success rate went from 82% -> 99% for inter-region mTLS within 12min. Will still do full remediation.

sanjay: Started rolling restart for model-router pods in eu-west with:
```bash
kubectl rollout restart deployment/model-router -n infra --context=eu-west-1
```
Will track mounts: `kubectl exec` and cat /var/run/secrets/internal-ca/version

olivia: Patching sidecar to TLS1.3 build queued, but rolling restart should normalize. Also adding a preflight check to alert if CA bundle mismatch detected at startup.

mira: Note for runbook update (security): must require 72h overlap where both old and new CA are trusted across all gateways and sidecars for cross-region rotates. Add KMS secret versioning steps and a checklist: update internal-ca in secret-store -> push to regions -> confirm mounts -> then rotate clients/servers.

julian: For TLS config hardening: create a compatibility matrix per service indicating min TLS version & ciphers supported. We'll fail closed in 7 days after matrix verified.

mira: Filing a tracking ticket with root cause and remediation steps, linking to incident channel and the audit logs we pulled. Ticket: https://tickets.rw/inc/4521 (internal).

certbot-bot: reminder: next automatic CA rotation scheduled in 90 days. Consider switching to gradual auto-overlap mode.

kai: Quick follow-up — we saw 3 nodes in eu-west still serving old certs because node-level sidecar injector cached images. I'll add a post-deploy hook to flush injector cache.

mira: Thanks everyone. Will update compliance checklist once we confirm no gaps in audit logging (RBAC for secret access, KMS decrypt events) and add a runbook step to notify eng-security on any CA rotate.

olivia: Closing the immediate incident. If anyone sees more TLS rejects ping here. :lock:
